annotations.closureRule: An END or CERT is an accepted predicate-conjunction leaf; JOIN is an accepted acyclic reference. OPEN is unresolved, never an accepted closure. No other annotation changes acceptance. Multiple accepted certificates at one endpoint are allowed. A continuing position cannot carry a closure.
annotations.nodeRule: Every position in a checkpoint PGN has exactly one explicit NODE anchor, unique within its game. It has no chess or acceptance authority.
annotations.userRule: USER records user-supplied moves, legally enumerated replies, or a selected/checked certificate, anchored to a same-game ancestor NODE. It never gives acceptance. No STOCKFISH attribution is generated for a user move. Existing engine provenance is retained.
annotations.classRule: CLASS optionally groups at least two legal sibling defenses at a defense parent in a tree or theorem application. Its three-word dictionary name identifies one signed recipe in the applicable dictionary scope. Any number of ordinary children may coexist with these groups; a one-member case is an ordinary child.
annotations.staticRule: STATIC records a dictionary-generated, independently checked application. One to three ordered applications may close through exactly Static endgame win or Static endgame reduction. Derived future guarantees never become current observations.

semanticChecks: Exact fixed tag roster/order and typed values; no unknown or duplicate tag.
Root annotations MAINLINE, PIECES and START occur once in this order and nowhere else.
Every byte is consumed: unknown keywords, predicates, theorem/terminal names, extra prose, NAGs, percent escape lines, semicolon comments, and unmatched delimiters are rejected.
Single numbered SAN ply per line; recursive opponent variations only; canonical LF/TAB wrapping; no arbitrary blank lines in movetext.

MAINLINE replays from FEN and equals the unvaried sequence, except a registered defensive-closure application or explicit preparation grouping may retain the frozen MAINLINE as an exact prefix of its extended unvaried analysis. All actual moves and numbers remain canonical.
Result header and final result agree; Player/Defense headers are reciprocal; PIECES case convention follows Player.
Root FEN and frozen Lichess mainline/final FEN match the source contract.
Every leaf is END/CERT/acyclic JOIN or explicitly OPEN; OPEN cannot coexist with an accepted endpoint; closure precedes no continuation.
The compiler obtains all acceptance from registered END/CERT applications or JOINs, never from prose, reasons, engine scores, UI evidence, or review-terminal side objects.

Every capture has an observed attack by the actual capturer on the actual physical target. Its observation may be earlier on this branch only if the relation remains true on every intervening position; en passant is explicit.

Only an explicit optional parent CLASS groups multiple defenses for storage. Its accepted signed recipe covers omitted continuations; a matching label or representative alone grants no acceptance. Ordinary stored children are raw even if their continuations look alike.

All retained concrete moves replay legally. At an expanded opposing parent, declared CLASS Members plus ungrouped direct children form a disjoint exact cover of the legal replies. With no CLASS, every legal reply is an ordinary stored child.
Every build/export/workshop path uses this locked specification and the same conformity gate; deterministic regeneration is required.

Every invoked Fork, Royal fork, Pin and Skewer has a previously OBSERVED bound geometry, continuously true through the entry position; a failed relation expires and cannot be revived without a new observation.

A move may clear an OBSERVED friendly obstruction and establish or exploit the resulting attack/alignment in the same ply. The prerequisite is the obstructed line before that move, never a retroactive observation.
Persistent preconditions are checked on all concrete class members, on standalone PGNs and on every workshop/export path. A shared piece type is not a shared physical identity.
Existing engine children are compressible; they do not protect an earlier position from an applicable END/CERT. Immutable reference continuations remain separately checked.
Every active theorem ID/name and ordered ENTRY/provenance expression must be in the human-approved registry. The catalogue and CFG share these exact definitions.
Every JOIN matches an approved source board, source node/application and target binding. Existing valid targets alone do not authorize new JOINs.
Every emitted mate_threat_in_2 predicate has a checked three-ply tree; every legal second-ply reply has an actual mating third ply. Threat projections never appear as null game moves.
Every position has one unique NODE anchor; all puzzle content comes exclusively from PGN text.

A declared parent CLASS stores one representative child for at least two legal members. All defenses outside declared groups are ordinary children with their actual continuations. No grouped nonrepresentative subtree is stored.
JOIN source and target records belong to the PGN; the definition file contains only the generic join contract. Workshop changes cannot invent/rebind an input JOIN.

USER sources resolve to this node or an ancestor in the same game; enum replies are opponent moves; selected/checked endpoints are existing named main certificate conjunctions and independently hold. No USER move lies on the frozen reference path.

Legacy child-attached gross T38 category labels are not accepted CLASS syntax in v16. T38 chess categories remain unchanged dictionary data; an unsupported theorem entry or grouping adapter rejects explicitly.
capture_reply_tree(K,6) applications are always independently checked, including applications without USER metadata. No new predicates or certificates are learned on import.

Every optional CLASS declaration is on the actual defense parent and names one direct-child representative with at least two Members. Singleton defenses are ordinary children. Group Members plus ordinary replies exhaust the legal move set; no duplicate member, extra grouped child or entry alias is allowed.

Every theorem ENTRY is checked on its attached board and bound recorded move. Required template conditions cannot be omitted or replaced by unrelated true atoms; every printed atom must hold. Reject unsupported templates and predicates. T39 ENTRY and every CLASS name and signed condition are generated exactly from the dictionary.

DictionarySHA256 equals the hash of the exact loaded dictionary bytes. PositionsExplored always equals the actual physical NODE records, partitioned once into raw nodes and explicit class representatives. Every stored node costs one.

Explicit Take / exchange preparation groups apply only after an actual legal player capture whose current board satisfies every preparation entry condition. Scope follows from that capture and matching dictionary class names, without a DEFINITION marker or extra ENTRY. Valid inherited facts need not be repeated in OBSERVED.

For groups that omit continuations, bind prior checked fit provenance and its evidence hash to the parent FEN, prover, original material baseline, class key and complete signed recipe member set. Verify every legal reply's signed predicates and all stored ordinary and representative endings; omitted group members need no universal future-subtree expansion.

CLASS is optional and uses a three-word dictionary name followed by separate Representative, Members, positive and negative predicate lines. Place one or more groups on the parent application. Every group has at least two members, exactly one stored direct-child representative, correct generated signs and disjoint complete coverage together with ordinary children.

Validate dictionary graph structure before applications: reachability, references, cycles, actor alternation, actual-ply depth, typed move edges, zero-ply cases and explicit exits. Only the four named atomic theorems may establish a result in one ply.
Check every END/CERT independently, also in games without CLASS. A same-board theorem handoff validates its complete dependency and rejects cycles.

A checking queen that can be captured selects the capturable case regardless of whether the capture is a profitable win or an equal exchange. Capturing the checker does not bypass recapture settlement or the existing ending check.
A PGN move number must match its actual parent board turn and fullmove number. Abstract case edges consume no physical move or position.

Every registered meta tree is a theorem. Its authoritative variable PGN must compile to its exact graph cache, its physical entry bindings and all matched node/exit predicates must hold, and its actual ply depth must meet the theorem contract. MOTIF is prohibited.

preconditionContract.scope: all captures by both sides and all invoked theorems; concrete members and PGN exports
preconditionContract.lifetime: observe once, carry while continuously true; expire at first false on this branch
preconditionContract.capture: exact physical capturer and target; attacks or explicit legal en-passant availability
preconditionContract.line: Skewer entry requires the observed alignment of the same two opposing targets before the attacker joins. Check the attacker-front-rear line after joining and the same rear capture after the reply. Other inherited geometry rules are unchanged.
preconditionContract.fork: piece-appropriate common attack geometry, not a forced straight line for knights or mixed slider rays
preconditionContract.promotion: promotion_fork_pattern explicitly identifies the pawn, promoted type and target pair
preconditionContract.noNewAcceptance: END/CERT/JOIN semantics unchanged; provenance and evidence have no acceptance authority
preconditionContract.inheritance: Validate every START and OBSERVED atom on its attached board. Add its actual physical bindings to the current branch. Carry each binding down that branch only while it remains true at every intervening board; expire it at the first false board. A fresh OBSERVED may establish a new source. No sibling or expired source is inherited.
preconditionContract.provenance: The validator derives the ancestor source, physical piece identities, and intervening board sequence. Captures consume an appropriate live observed capture relation. A theorem root is observed either by its checked physical ENTRY on that board or by an appropriate live inherited START/OBSERVED relation that is rechecked there. Every subsequent theorem node rechecks its listed requirements with those physical bindings; another same-type piece cannot silently replace a bound piece.
preconditionContract.unknown: Reject unsupported START/OBSERVED predicates instead of treating an unimplemented fact as true.

theorems.replies: Follow the recorded main line through the stated actual plies. Printed PGN variations state additional admitted outcomes. Other defenses stay in the concrete puzzle tree and may have their own theorem or accepted CLASS.
theorems.proof: The entry is checked on the starting board with physical piece identities. Replay each numbered variable move as exactly one adjacent legal ply; check every intermediate and exit condition again on the matched board. A theorem result supplies the next facts. An EXIT certificate requires an independently accepted END/CERT on that same board.

Otherwise explicit CLASS groups after an actual legal player capture may use the unique matching capture-preparation contract and its checked entry conditions. A later theorem application may have its own optional groups on the existing position; no extra scope marker or entry-alias node is needed. The canonical theorem can refine a storage recipe with zero-ply signed cases; these abstract cases do not create stored representatives or change the accepted Members binding.
classContract.acceptance: Entry truth, signed membership, accepted recipe authorization for omitted continuations, and every stored continuation remain separate checks. CLASS is optional storage grouping. A fully expanded application needs no elision authorization but still checks its actual entries, legal coverage, signed recipes and retained endings.
classContract.textIntegrity: Generate every class name and signed condition from the dictionary. The PGN supplies only board bindings, Representative and Members. Descriptions and recipes remain dictionary data, not DEFINITION annotations. Reject edited or stale class text. For So what, the concrete bindings additionally identify its fixed Plan UCI and exact registered Exit certificate ID; their meaning and all explanatory text come from soWhatContract.

theoremTreeContract.meaning: Every registered meta tree is a theorem. Its authoritative source is PGN-shaped move text with physical piece variables; compiling it gives a finite abstract tree or shared-node DAG fitted to adjacent actual game positions. Node predicates state necessary facts, and each leaf explicitly returns checked facts, an existing accepted certificate, or a completely checked next theorem.
theoremTreeContract.nodeSemantics: Conjoin predicates; negate each negative expression as a whole. Evaluate all atom implementations before Boolean short-circuiting. Recheck at each mapped board; inherited observations retain their physical identity and expiry rules.

edgeSemantics.ply: Exactly one adjacent legal move shown by its variable-PGN number, declared actor, optional physical mover and capture target, and any/capture/check/mate constraint.
edgeSemantics.class: Zero plies on the same physical board; exactly one signed case applies. A case may refer to an existing dictionary class definition. It cannot contain a move or inflate depth.

theoremTreeContract.depth: Only Mate, Take / exchange, Check, and Mate threat are atomic one-ply theorems. Every compound source contains a core spanning at least two actual plies, and every ordinary theorem-result exit requires at least two. A shorter branch may stop only at an explicit independently accepted END/CERT or checked handoff after its stated local facts actually hold; no unperformed reply is claimed.
graphChecks: Exactly one root; every node reachable
Acyclic graph and finite application dependencies
Consistent alternating actors across all paths
No mixed class/ply edges at one node
No ambiguous or missing actual case
Every named theorem source compiles to the exact cached graph
Mainline templates map the recorded main line; all-defenses templates require every actual defense or an existing checked CLASS member binding

A class-members tree has an explicit registered classScope, a defender root and at least two actual plies on every path to an exit; its matching checked concrete CLASS fixes membership, Plan and Exit. Validate every member against the declared graph and independently validate full parent coverage and ordinary exceptions.

exitSemantics.theorem: The declared local result holds here. It supplies no END/CERT authority by itself.
exitSemantics.certificate: An existing END/CERT on this same actual board is independently checked. For a matching checked So what CLASS, its fixed registered Exit may instead supply theorem-local certificate evidence: re-evaluate that same unchanged certificate at this actual second-ply board for every member, including when the stored main line continues.
exitSemantics.handoff: An existing checked ending or another completely matched ENTRY on this same board. No skipped moves, implicit future ending, unsupported application, or cyclic dependency.

derivedPredicateDefinitions.sole_checking_piece(S): On this side-to-move board, enumerate legal checking replies and identify their actual checking physical pieces after each reply. Their nonempty union must be exactly the bound opposing piece S. The printed q form requires the unique opposing queen.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.checker(S,K): The same still-present physical piece S currently attacks the player king.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.checker_capturable(S): The same physical piece S is checking the player king and at least one currently legal player move captures it. Negation denies that entire existence; capture profitability is separate.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.captured(A): The bound original physical identity has been captured on the mapped path and is absent from this board.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.moved(A): The incoming actual move was made by the same bound physical identity A.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.aligned(B,C): The two distinct physical targets lie on one file, rank or diagonal; this entry relation does not require A already on the line.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.line(A,B,C): The same slider A has B in front of C on a compatible ray with no other blocker between A and C.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.accepted_ending: Validation service: an existing same-board END/CERT independently holds. This is not an Oracle board predicate or a new certificate.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.validated_entry: Validation service: a different same-board ENTRY has its whole tree checked without a dependency cycle. This is not an inherited board fact.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.route(A;EXPR): There exists one legal move by the bound A, viewed with A’s side to move and en-passant cleared only when that view changes turns, whose resulting board satisfies EXPR with the same physical bindings. Nested route describes geometric accessibility, never an unplayed actual ply or an opponent pass. King-capture pseudo-moves are excluded.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.distinct(A,B): The two bound physical identities differ. This explicit predicate prevents aliasing where the theorem requires separate targets.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.value(A)>value(B): Compare the material point scale pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9, king 0, using the same scale as existing concrete ENTRY checks. Zero is the king’s ledger contribution, never permission to capture a king or make an illegal king move. Pin tests explicitly give the rear king royal priority separately from this material comparison.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.pawn(P): The bound present piece currently has pawn type.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.passed(P): The bound present pawn has no opposing pawn ahead of it on its own or either adjacent file.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.near_promotion(P): The bound present pawn is on White’s sixth or seventh rank, or Black’s third or second rank. This is an entry fact, not a promotion guarantee.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.pawn_step_clear(P): The immediate forward square of the bound present pawn lies on the board and is empty.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.pawn_step_blocked(P,B): The same bound physical B occupies the immediate forward square of the bound pawn P.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.controls_step(A,P): The bound A geometrically controls the bound pawn P’s immediate forward square on the current board.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.controls_promotion(A,P): The bound A geometrically controls the promotion square on the bound pawn P’s current file, using P’s color to choose the promotion rank.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.pawn_chain(P,Q): P and Q are distinct same-side present pawns, and the base P geometrically defends Q’s occupied square.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.adjacent_majority(P,Q,D): Distinct friendly pawns P and Q occupy adjacent files. D is an opposing pawn on one of those files and ahead of both. In those files and their neighboring files, D is the only opposing pawn ahead of the less advanced friendly pawn. This exact local two-against-one observation supplies entry only.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.opposition(H,J): The bound opposing kings lie on the same rank or file at distance two, with exactly one intervening square. Actual side to move is separately supplied by the node and move numbering.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.closer(H,P): Both the same king H and same pawn P remain present. Their current Chebyshev distance is strictly less than at this theorem application’s entry.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.promoted(P): P is the same physical identity that was a pawn at entry, remains on the board, and now has queen, rook, bishop, or knight type.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.pins(A,B,C): The bound player slider A, opposing front piece B, and opposing rear piece C form the checked line(A,B,C), with C the king or more valuable than B.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.defended(A): At least one distinct same-side piece geometrically guards the bound present A on this board.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.valuable_attack(A): The present bound A geometrically attacks at least one actual opposing non-king piece of strictly greater material value on the current board, using pawn 1, knight/bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9, king 0. Evidence identifies A and every qualifying target. This existential current-board attack is not a claim of legal capture, a binding to a future target, piece safety, or a forced gain; a counterattack continuation requires a checked handoff or independently accepted ending.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.blocks(M,D): The bound player M occupies the next square of the friendly pawn D, or is the sole intermediate blocker on a compatible ray between the friendly slider D and a present opposing target. The exact entry relationship is retained for cleared(M,D).
derivedPredicateDefinitions.cleared(M,D): Recheck the exact entry relationship from blocks(M,D): for a pawn, the same pawn’s original immediate forward square is empty; for a slider, the same slider now attacks the same originally blocked opposing target. No unrelated newly clear line can substitute.
derivedPredicateDefinitions.endgame: Both queens are absent, or combined non-pawn material excluding kings is no greater than the existing configured endgame threshold. This observation has no closing authority.

theoremTreeContract.provenance: Every theorem entry is an actual checked observation of its exact physical root bindings before the first consuming ply. Existing inherited observations remain valid when their same physical relation survives. In particular, Skewer cannot enter unless the same target alignment is observed at its root or remains live from an ancestor. Capture preparation continues to use the inherited observation contract.
theoremTreeContract.classesAndCounting: Abstract cases map existing boards and are not PGN CLASS declarations. Only an actual printed multi-member CLASS has a stored representative; every stored NODE is counted exactly once. No future omitted member positions are inserted by the matcher.
theoremTreeContract.implementationBoundary: The standalone validator, corpus importer, and Atlas use the same variable-PGN compiler, board predicates, entry gate, and complete matcher for all 33 theorem definitions. Dictionary diagrams derive from that checked graph, and puzzle overlays derive from actual validated applications.

source.compiledCache: registry.theorems[].tree; its node/edge graph must equal the compilation of metaPgn
source.bindings: tree.variables supplies player/opponent/either-side physical piece types; entryExplanation and bindingNotes explain the observed binding relationships in plain English.
source.numbering: x1., x1..., x2., x2... count real plies relative to entry. A defender-to-move entry starts x1... .

moves.A ~: One actual legal move by the bound A.
moves.A x B: One actual legal capture of the bound B by the bound A.
moves.A +: One actual legal checking move by A.
moves.A #: One actual legal mating move by A.
moves.*: An unconstrained actual mover or capture target; it does not skip a ply.

source.comments: NODE/REF anchors, optional TURN, required + predicates, forbidden - predicates, and explicit EXIT theorem/certificate/handoff directives. Boolean all(...; ...), any(...; ...), and not(...) are parsed expressions. PGN parentheses contain alternative branches.
source.classes: CLASS names a same-board signed alternative when a defense recipe needs it. It adds zero real plies and zero concrete positions. Only a concrete multi-member CLASS declaration supplies a stored representative; ordinary conditional early endings use PGN variations.
source.integrity: Compile and compare the whole source graph, not merely its label or a rendered explanation. Reject missing source, skipped/renumbered plies, unknown bindings or predicates, cycles, unreachable nodes, ambiguous matched branches, missing exits, and a changed compiled cache.

theoremTreeContract.coverage: Ordinary theorem templates fit the recorded main line, with optional explicit PGN variations. This does not close other concrete defenses or turn them into explored representatives. An all-defenses template, including Single-queen defensive closure, additionally matches the accepted concrete CLASS partition and its existing representative recipe boundary. A class-members template covers exactly the members of its registered classScope at the actual entry parent. Require that matching checked CLASS, preserve its fixed physical plan and exit bindings, and match the full declared graph for every member. This scoped theorem does not close ordinary exceptions.
theoremTreeContract.staticException: The explicitly separate static-endgame schema permits same-node derivations with zero consumed plies. This does not change atomic exceptions, compound depth, all-defenses coverage or CLASS accounting for any dynamic theorem.

soWhatContract.name: So what
soWhatContract.shortDefinition: For every defense in this class, play the same physically bound move and check the same existing terminal certificate on the resulting board. Keep one concrete representative and its player continuation; handle every other defense separately.

actor.source: The piece on the fixed Plan source square at this actual entry board.

entry.meaning: The opponent is to move and the player piece bound as A exists. Instantiate the printed piece role from Plan, then bind A to that exact physical entry identity. Check these board facts before either numbered ply.
entry.nonterminal: Entry and the member defense board must permit the next actual legal ply. A game-ending defense cannot be ignored.

plan.binding: Fix one legal reference defense, one canonical UCI player move and one registered terminal certificate before testing membership. The Plan source, destination and promotion choice, physical actor and any physical captured target are fixed for the whole class.
plan.physicalIdentity: The actor and any captured target must already exist at entry and keep their identities through the defense. The same destination occupied by a different target does not satisfy the plan. Canonical SAN may gain or lose a check suffix; the fixed UCI and physical bindings remain unchanged.
plan.validation: After every selected legal defense, the same bound player move must be legal, including all king-safety and promotion requirements. It must answer an actual check if the defense checks. Re-evaluate all declared intermediate and exit predicates on that member's actual boards.
plan.scope: This first implementation supports exactly one player move after the wildcard defense. A longer plan needs a fully checked strategy subtree including every newly available opposing reply; principal-variation survival alone is insufficient.

classes.label: Main plan survives
classes.shortDefinition: Whatever listed defense is played, the same fixed player move remains legal and reaches the same checked terminal certificate.

bindings.A: The one physical player piece fixed by the parent Plan source square. Never rebind A to a different piece on another member.

obligations: Members contains at least two distinct legal sibling defenses and includes the one stored Representative exactly once.

For each listed member, replay the actual defense and the exact fixed Plan with the same physical actor, target if captured, and promotion choice. Check the signed predicates on the immediate defense board.

Re-evaluate the exact existing certificate selected by Exit at every resulting second-ply board. Its original conjunction, original puzzle material baseline and relevant actual history remain unchanged.
Check the complete declared variable-PGN graph, including all intermediate predicates and its explicit certificate exit, for the representative and every replayed member.
A legal Plan without the required certificate is a continuation-only result and cannot authorize this terminal CLASS. Any failed or unproved defense stays outside the class.

Store only one defense representative and its actual player continuation for this group. Keep every exception as an ordinary child or a separately authorized class; count every stored board exactly once.

soWhatContract.signedPredicates: Positive and negative expressions are checked on each immediate defense board with the same physically bound A. These visible board signs are necessary conditions, not a substitute for the two-ply plan and terminal certificate obligations.
soWhatContract.partition: The declared class may be any proved subset of the legal defenses. Its members and all ungrouped direct-child defenses form a disjoint exact legal cover. A proved but unselected defense may remain ordinary. Exceptions receive no closure from T40. An empty class is invalid; a singleton is an ordinary child.
soWhatContract.quantifiers: Choose the bound Plan and exact Exit first. For every defense d in the declared Members, d is legal at entry, Plan is legal after d with the same physical bindings, and Exit holds after d followed by Plan. Do not choose a different plan or exit independently for each defense.
soWhatContract.classAuthorization: Derive authority by replaying every actual member with the fixed plan and unchanged certificate at validation time. No accepted-position list, matching label, successful representative alone or newly invented plan-success predicate grants elision.

exit.selection: Exit is the exact ID of one existing registered main terminal certificate; its name, atoms and parameters are obtained from the dictionary and cannot be weakened or replaced while testing members.
exit.anchors: Use the original puzzle root and its actual root-to-entry move history for every replay. Preserve its player, material baseline, physical identities and any history-sensitive chess state. Reject terminal draws under the current chess rules.
exit.local: The certificate is checked at the actual second-ply board. It may be theorem-local evidence supplied by CLASS Exit when the stored main line continues. It does not insert a fictitious END, skip any later stored moves, remove their OPEN obligations or claim the surrounding puzzle complete.
exit.existingSemantics: This theorem adds no terminal certificate and changes no condition of an existing ending. Checking the same registered conjunction for every member is mandatory.

tree.shape: One wildcard opposing ply, then the fixed player Plan, then the explicitly checked certificate exit.
tree.scope: Only the declared members are mapped by this theorem application. The parent's full legal coverage and all ordinary exceptions are validated independently.

soWhatContract.accounting: A CLASS consumes zero plies and has one stored defense representative. Its actual player response is another stored position; ordinary exceptions and any later stored continuations also count. Report membership replays and certificate-internal work separately from stored positions; compression does not imply only one board was checked.

integrity.text: Render the name, definitions, class signs and field layout from this dictionary. The PGN supplies only concrete entry/plan/exit bindings, Representative and Members. Reject stale or edited explanatory class text.

staticTheoremContract.meaning: A checked same-node implication over a current position or a universal outcome envelope. It adds zero concrete PGN nodes and zero CLASS representatives. Each theorem has explicit checked entry and one to three outputs. At most three applications compose into the registered terminal certificate.
staticTheoremContract.source: registry.staticTheorems[].metaPgn is a zero-ply variable-PGN source with one existing-position root and no edges. Its entry and derivation exit must compile exactly to its cached static tree. Dynamic theorem depth and coverage rules remain unchanged.
staticTheoremContract.entry: Validate the actual FEN, side, physical piece bindings, legal live status, clock and recorded branch history. Recompute every geometric or explicitly bounded move-effect obligation. For a derived region, quantify over all represented outcomes and preserve the source, player, physical actor, kings, material baseline and strategy.
staticTheoremContract.composition: The first step reads the current board. Each later step consumes only the immediately preceding checked envelope from this same ordered chain. No rebinding, skipped premise, cycles, independently chosen existential outcomes, or future fact inherited as a current board observation.

terminal.name: Static endgame win
terminal.semantics: The position admits a forced conversion to an elementary winning major-piece ending under the usual root-relative puzzle convention. It does not assert that mate or promotion already occurred. Prior history before the supplied root FEN is unavailable; this certificate is a theoretical endgame result, not a reconstruction of all possible earlier draw claims.

staticTheoremContract.history: Reject a repeated canonical position in the recorded branch, a current drawn/terminal entry, en-passant/castling outside the scope, or entry/endpoint halfmove clock above 50. Fixed corridors cannot revisit unchanged friendly placements. No claim is made about unrecorded pre-root history.

accounting.testing: Independent concrete-reply replay, randomized legal positions and KPK retrograde checks are offline tests. No engine, tablebase or diagnostic search is a runtime dependency. Entry legality uses the existing chess rules. Mask theorem variants operate on conservative regions; bounded effect variants explicitly inspect hypothetical legal continuations of a fixed plan and report that work. Neither adds a concrete corpus node.

outputPredicates.forces_key_position(P): Universal future envelope with the same surviving pawn, exact player king square, possible defending-king region, side to move, and clock.
outputPredicates.forces_capture(p): The declared blocked opposing pawn is captured on the same corridor that produces the key envelope.
outputPredicates.forces_pawn_survival(P): The bound player pawn survives all defenses represented by that same corridor.
outputPredicates.forces_safe_major_promotion(P): There exists one strategy that guarantees a queen or rook promotion which is not immediately capturable and does not stalemate; the defending side has no remaining pawn or piece.
outputPredicates.theoretical_win(K): A future theoretical win established through the checked promotion envelope and elementary major-piece conversion. Never a current-board mate observation.
outputPredicates.forces_pawn_ending_region(P): One same-strategy universal pawn/king or promotion region, with piece-square masks, optional captures, side, clock, bindings and live-state guards. A guarded bare-king subprocedure may further establish safe major promotion.
outputPredicates.forces_queen_ending_region(A): One same-strategy universal region after checked queen control or collection, preserving every surviving opposing pawn and piece.
outputPredicates.forces_guarded_promotion_region(P): A promotion region whose full checking/nonchecking partition, legal continuations and material/draw bounds have been proved by the declared mask or bounded effect variant.
outputPredicates.forces_accepted_ending(K): Every outcome of the linked checked region meets an explicitly declared registered ending. This is future strategy evidence, never an OBSERVED or START fact.

rendering.template: STATIC "{name}": Bind {bindings}; Entry {entry}; Output {output}; Plan {witness}; Proof {proof}.
rendering.source: Names, entry/output predicates and layout come from this dictionary. Physical bindings, plan and digest are recomputed; altered wording, order, predicates, plan or hash is rejected.

terminals.name: Static endgame win
terminals.semantics: The position admits a forced conversion to an elementary winning major-piece ending under the usual root-relative puzzle convention. It does not assert that mate or promotion already occurred. Prior history before the supplied root FEN is unavailable; this certificate is a theoretical endgame result, not a reconstruction of all possible earlier draw claims.

terminals.name: Static endgame reduction
terminals.semantics: A checked strategy forces one of the explicitly named registered puzzle endings. The boundary may be a material objective rather than a forced-mate theorem. It never supplies a current mate observation.

adjacent_pawn_majority.meaning: Counts friendly and opposing pawns in the adjacent-file group used as a majority-breakthrough entry. A count is a recognition cue, not a win.

aligned.meaning: The two bound targets already share the given rank, file or diagonal before the consuming move.

alignment.meaning: Three successive occupied squares on the indicated ray type; endpoint colors differ and at least one endpoint is a slider for that direction. Reversal is canonicalized.

attacked.meaning: An occupied piece of the named type is attacked by the shown multiset of enemy piece types. Geometric attacks include pinned pieces.

attacked_count.meaning: Number of pieces of the named relative role attacked by opposing pieces on the current board.

attacks.meaning: At the recorded board, the physical piece bound to A geometrically attacks the piece bound to b. Squares and stable identities are evidence, not parts of certificate predicates.

base_defended.meaning: The named bishop defends the bound pawn-chain base.

blockaded_near_pawn_count.meaning: Number of bound near-promoting pawns whose next advance square is occupied by an effective friendly blocker.

capture_moves.meaning: The named side has exactly n legal captures, including en passant; n is positive.

capture_promoted_piece.meaning: Count of legal immediate captures of the newly promoted piece in the checked continuation.

capture_value.meaning: Maximum immediate opposing capture loss, compared with the exact declared material-gain margin. This is a bounded board test, not a whole-game guarantee.

castling_path_clear.meaning: The required squares between the king and rook are empty for the indicated castling side.

castling_path_safe.meaning: The available castling move has a safe initial king square, transit square and destination.

castling_right.meaning: The FEN retains the named side’s indicated castling right. Castling is a move type, not a theorem.

check.meaning: The named side is in check.

check_moves.meaning: The side named by king K has exactly n legal checking moves; n is positive.

controlled_promotion_count.meaning: Number of near-promoting opposing pawns with a bound, legally effective promotion-square controller.

counterchecks.meaning: Number of legal opposing checking replies in the explicitly evaluated reply set.

defended_count.meaning: Number of pieces of the named role defended by a friendly piece.

defenders.meaning: An attacked non-king piece of this type has exactly n same-color geometric defenders.

defends.meaning: The first named friendly piece attacks the square occupied by the second named friendly piece.

distance.meaning: The indicated king and a pawn of the indicated side are n king steps apart, ignoring obstacles.

distance_count.meaning: Exactly c pawns of the indicated side are n king steps from this king.

distance_to_promotion.meaning: The king is n king steps from the pawn’s promotion square.

distance_to_step.meaning: The king is n king steps from the pawn’s next advance square.

double_attack_moves.meaning: Exactly n legal moves by the named side make the moved piece geometrically attack at least two occupied enemy squares.

en_passant_available.meaning: A legal en-passant capture of the identified pawn is available. The captured pawn and landing square differ; no attack on an occupied landing square is fabricated.

endgame.meaning: Both queens are absent, or total non-pawn material excluding kings is no greater than the configured endgame threshold. This activates observations; it does not close a leaf.
endgame.theoremMeaning: Both queens are absent, or combined non-pawn material excluding kings is no greater than the existing configured endgame threshold. This observation has no closing authority.

evasion_captures.meaning: Number of legal check evasions that capture.

evasion_promotions.meaning: Number of legal check evasions that promote.

fork_moves.meaning: The side named by king K has a legal move whose moved piece geometrically attacks at least two enemy targets valued at least three, or the king.

fork_pattern.meaning: The same two surviving target pieces already occupy a geometric attack pattern for A before the move. The candidate destination is retained only as bound evidence.

hang.meaning: A non-king of this piece type has at least one geometric attacker, no pawn defender, and strictly more attackers than defenders.

has_captures.meaning: The named side is to move and has at least one, or no, legal capture.

has_checks.meaning: The named side is to move and has at least one, or no, legal checking move.

has_mate_in_1.meaning: At least one legal move for the named side immediately checkmates.

in_check.meaning: The named king is in check; its side is to move.

king_controls_promotion.meaning: The bound king controls the bound pawn’s promotion square.

king_defends.meaning: The bound king defends the named friendly piece or pawn.

king_distance.meaning: Chebyshev distance between the two kings, ignoring occupied and attacked transit squares.

legal.meaning: The named capture is legal on the current before-move board.

legal_blockade_move.meaning: A bound legal move occupies the near-promoting pawn’s next advance square.

legal_capture.meaning: The bound capturing piece can legally capture the bound target now.

legal_check.meaning: A legal candidate move by the bound piece gives check.

legal_escort_move.meaning: A legal king move reaches the bound passer’s escort square. Its subsequent route is a separate theorem tree.

legal_holding_move.meaning: A concrete legal move preserving the stated ending conditions exists; not an assumed pass.

legal_mate.meaning: A legal candidate move by the bound piece immediately checkmates.

legal_move.meaning: The bound candidate move by this role is legal.

legal_moves.meaning: The side to move, named by its king, has exactly n legal moves.

legal_pawn_advance.meaning: The bound pawn has the stated legal advance.

legal_promotion.meaning: The bound pawn can legally promote to the named piece type.

line.meaning: The bound three pieces lie on the relevant rank, file or diagonal, in the recorded order.

line_blocker.meaning: A piece of this type is the middle occupied square of an emitted three-piece alignment of the indicated ray type.

loose.meaning: A non-king of this piece type has equal nonzero geometric attacker and defender counts, with no pawn defender.

mate_in_1.meaning: The side named by king K has at least one legal move that checkmates immediately. The move itself is not part of the predicate.

material.meaning: Current material balance for the player: own minus opponent values, pawn 1, knight/bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9; kings 0. Not a board or path identity.

material_balance.meaning: Current material of the named side minus its opponent using P=1, N=B=3, R=5, Q=9; kings excluded.

mobility.meaning: A piece of type A on the side to move has exactly n legal moves.

near_promotion.meaning: An opponent pawn is one or two straight advances from promotion and every square straight ahead to promotion is empty. Its absence is required by quiet(k).
near_promotion.theoremMeaning: The bound present pawn is on White’s sixth or seventh rank, or Black’s third or second rank. This is an entry fact, not a promotion guarantee.

near_promotion_count.meaning: Number of bound opposing pawns within the configured advancement distance of promotion.

net_gain.meaning: Values P=1, N=B=3, R=5, Q=9, K=0. Net gain = (own minus opponent now) minus (own minus opponent at the puzzle start). The root is not reset at a theorem join or a defense nub.

net_gain_after.meaning: Material gain after the explicitly checked immediate continuation, measured from the puzzle’s starting balance.

no_captures.meaning: The named side has no legal captures in the specified current-board view.

no_checks.meaning: The named side has no legal checking move in the specified current-board view.

no_mate_in_1.meaning: The named side has no legal move that immediately checkmates.

non_pawn_material.meaning: Total point value of all knights, bishops, rooks and queens of both colors. Excludes pawns and kings.

nonpromotion_checks.meaning: Number of legal checks that are not promotion moves.

open_step.meaning: The bound pawn’s next forward square is empty.

opposed_pawns.meaning: Opposing bound pawns face one another in the specified pawn lock.

overloaded.meaning: One named defender guards n targets satisfying hang or loose. This is a duty count, not proof that both cannot be defended.

passed.meaning: The bound pawn has no enemy pawn ahead on its own or either neighboring file.
passed.theoremMeaning: The bound present pawn has no opposing pawn ahead of it on its own or either adjacent file.

passed_pawn.meaning: A passed pawn on White rank 6 or beyond, or Black rank 3 or beyond, as in the source. No opposing pawn lies ahead on its file or either adjacent file.

pawn.meaning: A pawn of the named relative role is present.
pawn.theoremMeaning: The bound present piece currently has pawn type.

pawn_box.meaning: Geometric pawn-box relation to the opposing king, accounting for the side to move. It is not a result against other pieces, blockers or checks.

pawn_chain.meaning: The first bound pawn defends the second bound friendly pawn.
pawn_chain.theoremMeaning: P and Q are distinct same-side present pawns, and the base P geometrically defends Q’s occupied square.

pawn_distances.meaning: Sorted advancement distances to promotion of pawns of the specified relative color.

pawn_lock.meaning: The bound opposing pawn structure blocks immediate advances.

pawn_route_blocked.meaning: At least one occupied square obstructs the bound pawn’s direct promotion route.

pawn_route_clear.meaning: No occupied square obstructs the bound pawn’s direct promotion route. Other interceptions remain separate.

pawn_same_rank.meaning: A player pawn and an opponent pawn occupy the same rank n files apart; no absolute square is named.

pawn_step_blocked.meaning: The first named pawn’s next advance square is occupied by the second bound piece.
pawn_step_blocked.theoremMeaning: The same bound physical B occupies the immediate forward square of the bound pawn P.

pawn_step_clear.meaning: The bound pawn’s next advance square is empty.
pawn_step_clear.theoremMeaning: The immediate forward square of the bound present pawn lies on the board and is empty.

piece.meaning: A piece of the named relative role is present.

piece_count.meaning: Exactly n pieces of the named side and type remain on the current board, including zero.

pin.meaning: A piece of the named type is the sole occupied square between its own king and an enemy slider on the same ray.

promoted.meaning: The recorded move has promoted the pawn to the specified piece.
promoted.theoremMeaning: P is the same physical identity that was a pawn at entry, remains on the board, and now has queen, rook, bishop, or knight type.

promotion_control_route.meaning: The supplied legal candidate adds control of the bound advanced opposing pawn’s promotion square.

promotion_distance.meaning: Number of rank advances from the bound pawn to its promotion rank; not a full race-time calculation.

promotion_distance_count.meaning: Exactly c pawns of that side stand n ranks short of promotion.

promotion_moves.meaning: The side named by king K has a legal promotion or a legal pawn move leaving the pawn passed. This does not assert forced promotion.

promotion_square_control.meaning: The first bound piece legally controls the second bound pawn’s promotion square.

queens_absent.meaning: Neither side has a queen on the current board.

quiet.meaning: Opponent to move, at least one legal move, not an immediate board-detectable draw, no legal move giving check, no legal capture, and no opponent pawn one or two ranks from promotion with every square straight ahead through the promotion square empty. A position may be reply-quiet while the opponent is in check: only the opponent’s available checks and captures are excluded. No additional not-in-check requirement is silently added.

reserve_step.meaning: In a king-and-pawn position, the supplied legal pawn step advances a reserve pawn behind a recorded fixed pawn lock.

rival_promotion_moves.meaning: Number of legal promotions available to the rival side in the specified reply position.

shared_defender.meaning: One named defender guards at least two targets with the shown type multiset, each satisfying hang or loose. Target multiplicity is retained.

skewer.meaning: An enemy slider meets the front and back targets successively; the front has higher nominal value. Geometry only, not a material guarantee.

sole_defender.meaning: Exactly one same-color geometric defender of the target exists; the target satisfies hang or loose.

support_route.meaning: For the supplied legal candidate, the move adds A as a geometric defender of the bound friendly piece B.

turn.meaning: The side named by K is to move. This guard is explicit, not an implicit admission filter.

two_step_attack_route.meaning: The candidate enters a clear slider route to the pre-existing line through the two bound targets. An obstructing reply remains a separate branch.

value.meaning: Piece value under the declared point scale; comparison concerns the named bound roles.
value.theoremMeaning: Compare the material point scale pawn 1, knight 3, bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9, king 0, using the same scale as existing concrete ENTRY checks. Zero is the king’s ledger contribution, never permission to capture a king or make an illegal king move. Pin tests explicitly give the rear king royal priority separately from this material comparison.

obstructed_alignment.meaning: A slider, two ordered opposing targets and a friendly obstruction are observed before the move. Removing that same obstruction can expose and exploit the line in one ply.

promotion_fork_pattern.meaning: Observed geometry for the bound pawn’s specified promotion type to attack both bound targets on promotion; the pawn is not treated as already promoted.

mate_threat_in_2.meaning: A concrete three-ply tree has one legal key, every legal defensive reply (at least one), and a legal checkmate after each reply. On defender-to-move boards, this is an explicitly labelled attacker-turn threat projection, not a played pass or unconditional win.

mating_route.meaning: A queen-key mate in one or two exists on the explicit attacker-turn projection of this board. It is a threat observation only; an intervening defender move must be checked on its actual board.

guarded_mating_route.meaning: The projected queen-key mating route is prevented by an opposing queen: removing that bound queen exposes a concrete mate in at most two. Queen removal is a conditional observation, never a played move or a winning certificate.

capture_reply_tree.meaning: The exact six-ply template in captureReplyContract succeeds. All current legal opponent checks/captures are considered. A check is answered only by a legal capture of its checking piece, or an existing terminal on that board; a capture by a recapture or, only if the gain is still >=2 and it was not check, a quiet holding move. Every branch ends at a pre-existing main certificate. Nonforcing play is the declared material-boundary assumption, not a universal whole-game proof.

route.meaning: There exists one legal move by the bound A, viewed with A’s side to move and en-passant cleared only when that view changes turns, whose resulting board satisfies EXPR with the same physical bindings. Nested route describes geometric accessibility, never an unplayed actual ply or an opponent pass. King-capture pseudo-moves are excluded.
route.theoremMeaning: There exists one legal move by the bound A, viewed with A’s side to move and en-passant cleared only when that view changes turns, whose resulting board satisfies EXPR with the same physical bindings. present.meaning: An explicitly parsed Boolean combination of registered physically bound theorem predicates. Every constituent is checked before the first ply.

blocks.meaning: The bound player M occupies the next square of the friendly pawn D, or is the sole intermediate blocker on a compatible ray between the friendly slider D and a present opposing target. The exact entry relationship is retained for cleared(M,D).

distinct.meaning: The two bound physical identities differ. This explicit predicate prevents aliasing where the theorem requires separate targets.
distinct.theoremMeaning: The two bound physical identities differ. This explicit predicate prevents aliasing where the theorem requires separate targets.

controls_promotion.theoremMeaning: The bound A geometrically controls the promotion square on the bound pawn P’s current file, using P’s color to choose the promotion rank.

controls_step.theoremMeaning: The bound A geometrically controls the bound pawn P’s immediate forward square on the current board.

closer.theoremMeaning: Both the same king H and same pawn P remain present. Their current Chebyshev distance is strictly less than at this theorem application’s entry.

pins.meaning: The bound player slider A, opposing front piece B, and opposing rear piece C form the checked line(A,B,C), with C the king or more valuable than B.

defended.meaning: At least one distinct same-side piece geometrically guards the bound present A on this board.
defended.theoremMeaning: At least one distinct same-side piece geometrically guards the bound present A on this board.

valuable_attack.meaning: The present bound A geometrically attacks at least one actual opposing non-king piece of strictly greater material value on the current board, using pawn 1, knight/bishop 3, rook 5, queen 9, king 0. This existential current-board attack is not a claim of legal capture, a binding to a future target, piece safety, or a forced gain; a counterattack continuation requires a checked handoff or independently accepted ending.

cleared.meaning: Recheck the exact entry relationship from blocks(M,D): for a pawn, the same pawn’s original immediate forward square is empty; for a slider, the same slider now attacks the same originally blocked opposing target. No unrelated newly clear line can substitute.
